factual_summaries.summary: GitHub Copilot for JetBrains added enterprise managed settings for plugin governance, MCP server allowlists, managed OpenTelemetry, and organization-controlled permission modes, including disabling approval bypass/autopilot behavior.

GitHub described portable Agent Plugins 1.0, Copilot app side chat for pending agent questions, Copilot CLI /tasks management, queued prompts and shell commands during an agent turn, plan plus autopilot headless mode, /rewind, and session-preserving /app handoff.

Agent Plugins 1.0 became generally available across VS Code, Copilot CLI, the Copilot SDK, and the Copilot app; the package format can bundle skills and MCP server configuration and can be governed with enterprise managed settings and MCP allowlists.

GitHub introduced organization-level rule insights in public preview, aggregating repository ruleset evaluations, failed and bypassed runs, filters, top bypassed repositories, and CSV export for reporting.
Axios reported that Google-created Agent2Agent Protocol is moving to the Agentic AI Foundation, alongside MCP, to advance neutral interoperability for communication among independent agents.

TechRadar argued that MCP is a connectivity/access layer, not a replacement for APIs or domain context, and that organizations still need governed data exposure, permissions, auditability, and matter-aware context.

TechRadar reported Linus Torvalds describing unusually large Linux 7.2 release candidates as a new normal driven by AI review tools producing bug reports, while humans still write, submit, and maintain the fixes.

Atlassian Feature Focus lists Rovo updates including A2A-based third-party agent connectivity, Rovo Insights for adoption visibility, and AI Access Controls for governing rollout pace and policy alignment.
Dust added configurable Slack auto-replies that let a Dust agent respond in a channel without an @mention, either to every message or only the first message in a new thread.

DevOps.com summarized a Wakefield/Sauce Labs survey: 80% of surveyed executives traced a production incident, outage, or customer-impacting defect to AI-generated code in the prior year, while only 6% said AI-generated code is tested with AI tools all the time or often.
